marks.gloss_en: the mishna: one who slaughters two heads at once -- his slaughter is valid
one who concealed the knife between the two simanim and severed the lower one -- his slaughter is not valid
Rav's ruling on a knife concealed beneath the hide, as the school of Rav transmit it: 'I do not know'
mishna: if one concealed the knife beneath the second siman and severed it, R' Yeshevav says the animal is a neveila (carcass)
the novelty of Rav's ruling over the mishna: even concealing top-down, in the manner of slaughter, disqualifies -- from the mishna alone one might have limited chalada to bottom-up cutting
מנהני מילי? אמר שמואל, דאמר קרא: חץ שחוט לשונם
Shmuel: [the source is] the verse 'their tongue is a shachut arrow, it speaks deceit'
תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל: ושחט -- אין ושחט אלא ומשך
ואומר: חץ שחוט לשונם מרמה דבר
the school of R' Yishmael: 'and he shall slaughter' (veshachat) means nothing other than 'and he shall draw'
מאי ואומר? וכי תימא זהב שחוט -- שנטווה כחוט הוא -- perhaps 'shachut gold' is gold spun like thread, and shows nothing about drawing
ודילמא עביד חלדה? -- perhaps the arrow cut [the simanim] concealed (chalada), which invalidates
Rava would examine an arrow for R' Yona bar Tachlifa
if he was slaughtering and severed two heads in one stroke: if the knife has [the length of] one full neck -- it is valid
